critical_code_review_comments: Materials.js openView() sets viewable in the success branch but never uses it (dead field); consider removing to reduce state shape confusion.

Backend GET /api/resources/{id}/file still accepts ?auth=<jwt> query param even though the new frontend no longer uses it. Since the JWT is a long-lived session token, leaving the query-token path enabled keeps tokens in server access logs / browser history. Recommend removing the query auth path or switching to short-lived signed download tokens.

URL.createObjectURL blob is revoked 4s after click for download; if user cancels the save dialog on slow disks the URL may still leak. Consider revoking on 'a.onclick' completion via requestIdleCallback or after 'downloadstart' event only.
seed_data_creation: During tests, created & then deleted: TEST *.png/pdf via backend suite; TEST QA Image, TEST QA PDF, QA PDF Alpha via Playwright (all cleaned via API DELETE at end).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Login route is /auth (NOT /login). Auth testids: tab-login/tab-register, email-input/password-input/auth-submit. Materials chapter folders render as [data-testid=folder-<chapterName>] and [data-testid=folder-General] for empty chapter. In-app viewer selector: [data-testid=material-viewer]; image -> img.src='blob:...'; PDF/txt -> iframe.src='blob:...'. Use precise [data-testid=view/download/delete-material-<id>] built from GET /api/resources ids -- 'has_text' filters can grab overlapping ancestor divs and cause overlay-intercepts-pointer errors when the viewer dialog is open. Backend GET /api/resources/{id}/file accepts BOTH Authorization: Bearer AND ?auth=<jwt>. Seed 'Chapter Notes' TXT under Electricity in Materials Batch may have been deleted across iterations; upload fresh test files as needed.
rca_of_the_issue: Reported AxiosError was due to the previous implementation opening resource URLs in a new tab / hitting the endpoint without Authorization when the browser followed the link. Fix migrates openView() and download() to authenticated axios GET with responseType:'blob' + URL.createObjectURL, wrapped in try/catch with toast.error(formatApiErrorDetail(...)). Verified: no AxiosError/console error in 3 different flows (image view, pdf view, download). Modal iframe/img consume blob URLs so no additional auth round-trip is needed by the browser, eliminating the class of error entirely.
